title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes
author: Priya Nambiar
summary: This document consolidates the product overview, high-level PRD requirements, design constraints, roadmap and themes, pricing & packaging notes, and the release notes for the Unified Inference product line. It is intended for product, engineering, sales, and customer success stakeholders planning the next 3-12 months of work and customer-facing launches.
goals: Provide a single, consistent API and operational model across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments
Reduce per-token inference cost by 30% for typical web-scale conversational workloads through batching, caching, and model routing
Enable enterprise-grade rollout controls (canary/A-B/fallback) with clear SLOs and observability
Ship packaging and pricing that supports self-serve PLG signups and a sales-assisted enterprise motion
non_goals: Replacing customer's full model training workflows (we focus on serving/inference, not training)
Becoming a one-size-fits-all solution for highly-customized on-prem hardware stacks in v1
key_use_cases: Consumer-facing chat: low-latency text generation with streaming and function/tool calling
Customer support automation: embeddings + reranking pipelines for retrieval-augmented generation
Product analytics and summarization: batch embeddings and low-cost bulk generation
Platform consolidation: single contract for hosted/dedicated/private deployment modes
requirements: REQ-01: Single REST/SDK API parity across Hosted, Dedicated, Private -- same request/response shapes and feature flags
REQ-02: Latency SLOs -- p95 <= 220ms for n=8 token generation (small models), configurable per-customer for Dedicated
REQ-03: Cost controls -- per-route batching, prefix caching, and quantization profile suggestions surfaced in Console
REQ-04: Rollouts -- support canary (10%) and A/B split (up to 50/50) with automatic rollback on quality regressions
REQ-05: Observability -- token-level cost, per-model latency histograms, tracing hooks, and prompt-level QA comparisons
REQ-06: Security & Compliance -- KMS integration, audit logging, VPC peering for Private deployments
REQ-07: Model variants -- automatic fallback to quantized or smaller compatible models when capacity constrained
success_metrics: Adoption: 30% of new customers enable Dedicated or Private within 6 months of sign-up
Performance: Average per-token cost reduced by 25% across top 10 customers using Optimize suggestions
Reliability: Platform-wide SLA attainment >= 99.95% over trailing 30 days for Hosted
Quality: Regression alerts triggered < 2% false-positive rate when evaluating against customer prompt sets
architecture_and_design_summary: Unified Inference combines a GPU-optimized serving runtime with a control plane that manages model routing, rollout policies, and observability. Key subsystems: (1) Serving runtime with continuous batching and KV cache; (2) Smart routing & policy engine; (3) Console & Optimize service for cost/perf recommendations; (4) Private control plane for VPC/on-prem deployments. See related architecture docs for diagrams and kernel selection rationale.
design_constraints: Must support heterogeneous GPU fleets (A100, H100, L4) with kernel selection by runtime
Backward-compatible API changes only via versioning and configurable client-side feature flags
Telemetry payloads must avoid PII and follow data-residency controls per customer
Rollout actions (canary, A/B, rollback) must complete within 5 minutes under normal load
roadmap_and_themes: Q2–Q3 2026: Stabilize v1 (hosted API parity, basic rollouts, Console observability). Q4 2026: Launch Redwood Optimize v2 (batching recommendations, quantization profiles) and Dedicated GA. Q1 2027: Private control plane beta with KMS/HSM integrations and enterprise packaging. Themes: Performance & Cost, Enterprise Readiness, Developer Velocity.
milestones: 2026-07-01: Dedicated beta (reserved capacity) with autoscaling primitives
2026-10-15: Redwood Optimize v2 GA with model & quantization suggestions
pricing_and_packaging_notes:
Pricing objectives: (1) Simple self-serve for developers with consumption-based units; (2) Predictable committed contracts for Dedicated; (3) Enterprise packaging for Private with platform fees and support tiers. Proposed pricing tiers (illustrative):

Pricing table (USD):
| Tier | Hosted | Dedicated | Private (on-prem) | Notes |
|------|--------|-----------|------------------|-------|
| Developer | $0.0008 / token | N/A | N/A | free trial credits and usage cap |
| Startup | $0.0006 / token + $50/mo | $2500/mo reserved pool | $10k onboarding + license | up to 100M tokens/mo |
| Enterprise | custom volume pricing | custom committed spend | custom + platform fee | includes SLA, SSO, audit logs |

Additional add-ons: extended observability retention, compliance evidence package, priority support. Discounts: annual commitments (10-20%), usage volume bands. Billing model: per-token + per-embedding unit; committed capacity billed monthly with overage at committed rate + 20%.
release_notes:
Release 2026.11.15 (Unified Inference):
- Features:
  - Unified REST/SDK API: streaming, function/tool calling, structured output support
  - Rollouts: canary and A/B split with automatic rollback on error-rate/latency regressions
  - Console: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency dashboard, and trace sampling hooks
  - Redwood Optimize v2: batching and quantization suggestions for top model families
- Performance improvements:
  - Continuous batching reduced average per-token GPU utilization by ~18% in benchmark suite
  - KV prefix caching reduced tail latency for common prompts by 12%
- Bug fixes:
  - Fixed race in cache eviction that caused stale KV entries under high throughput
  - Resolved SDK streaming disconnects when using HTTP/2 with certain proxies
- Known issues:
  - Private control plane beta: automated upgrades not yet supported (manual patching required)
  - Dedicated autoscaler can under-react to bursty short-lived spikes; mitigation document in eng-sre runbooks
rollout_and_deployment_plan: 1) Internal dogfood: 4-week trial across Platform and Growth teams, gather telemetry and prompt sets
2) Selected customers: invite-only beta for Dedicated (3 customers) and Private (1 regulated customer)
3) Gradual public rollout: enable new features by default for Developer & Startup tiers after 2 weeks of beta stability
4) Post-launch: 30-day monitoring window; auto-rollback thresholds tuned by engineering on first 7 days

operational_impact_and_slos: Primary SLOs: Hosted API availability 99.95% monthly; p99 generation latency targets published per model. Operational changes: new dashboards in Grafana (per-route latency + cost), two new alerts: (1) sustained p95 latency > target for 10 minutes, (2) token-cost anomaly > 20% vs baseline. Runbooks: see eng-sre/runbooks/unified-inference-ops
qa_and_regression_strategy: Every rollout must include a regression-suite run against representative prompt sets (customer-owned and Redwood canonical). Regression criteria: automatic rollback if response-quality metric (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity) drops > 3% on critical prompt set. Post-deploy: weekly sampling audits for first month.
faq:
Q: How does Unified Inference differ from prior Redwood hosted endpoints?
A: Unified Inference adds a consistent runtime and control plane across deployment modes, first-class rollouts, and Optimize-driven cost recommendations; API compatibility is maintained.

Q: What pricing should enterprise customers expect?
A: Enterprise customers receive bespoke pricing based on committed spend and desired SLAs; expect platform fees for Private deployments and options for multi-year discounts.

Q: How do rollbacks work?
A: Rollbacks are automated when configured triggers fire (latency, error rate, or quality regression). Manual rollback is available in Console with audit logging.
